mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between HOUST declines and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to improved economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a rise in real GDP (GDPC1) signals accommodative monetary policy in a growing economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% and GDPC1 increases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS decrease and GDPC1 increase on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of RSAFS increase and UNRATE decrease on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS declines and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) in a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
